name: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) Preliminaries
definition: Scene representation using a set of 3D points with anisotropic Gaussian extent as a proxy for geometry, where each Gaussian is cut at 3σ to form ellipsoid-shaped splats.
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting is a differentiable, point-based scene representation that replaces NeRF's implicit MLPs with explicit 3D Gaussians, enabling real-time high-fidelity novel view synthesis via GPU-friendly tile-based rasterization.
